steps.description: Build a DESeqDataSet from the raw integer counts and the metadata with design ~condition, setting the control level as the reference so log2 fold changes read as lesional-vs-control. steps.name: Leave-one-out sensitivity excluding sample_01
caveats: Removing one sample from a 6-vs-6 design reduces power in one arm, so some loss of significant genes is expected purely from n and is not evidence that sample_01 was driving a false signal — interpret via LFC concordance, not via the count of significant genes alone.
With 5 samples in one arm, dispersion estimates get noisier; do not over-read small shifts in padj.
steps.context: This is a robustness check on the primary result from T1S2, driven by the profiled caveat that sample_01 has ~4x below-median depth. It is not a replacement analysis: the reported gene list remains the full-cohort one unless T1S1 gave clear evidence of a degraded library.
steps.question: How much does the shallow sample_01 influence the lesional-vs-control gene list — do the DE calls and effect sizes hold when it is removed?
constraints: Use exactly the same filtering rule, design, and shrinkage method as T1S2 so the two runs are comparable; do not re-tune anything.
Report the resulting per-group sample sizes explicitly — the comparison becomes unbalanced.
Do not overwrite or replace the T1S2 primary results; this run is reported alongside them.
Correlate LFCs only over genes tested in both runs, and report how many genes that is.
steps.description: Re-run the identical DESeq2 workflow from T1S2 (same pre-filtering rule, same ~condition design, same shrinkage) on the 11 samples remaining after excluding sample_01, giving an unbalanced 5-vs-6 or 6-vs-5 contrast depending on sample_01's group — state which group it came from and the resulting group sizes. An explicit list of significance-status-changing genes.

steps.name: Hallmark pathway GSEA on the lesional-vs-control ranking
caveats: GSEA p-values on a 12,000-gene pre-filtered matrix are computed over a reduced universe; hallmark sets with low coverage in this matrix should be flagged rather than interpreted at face value.

Hallmark sets overlap in membership (notably the inflammatory / TNFA / interferon sets), so several correlated significant hits can reflect one underlying signal — inspect leading-edge overlap before claiming multiple independent pathways.
With n=6 per group the ranking is noisy at the tails; the NES ordering is more trustworthy than exact adjusted p-values.
Enrichment identifies coordinate expression shifts, not mechanism or causality — do not phrase results as pathway activation without independent evidence.
steps.context: Input is the ranked gene statistic from the DESeq2 lesional-vs-control contrast (T1S2) and the corresponding leave-one-out ranking (T1S3). The MSigDB human hallmark GMT is confirmed present in the environment's reference store for Homo sapiens, matching this dataset's organism. Hallmark is deliberately the requested collection: 50 broad, non-redundant states, appropriate for an n=6-per-group study where finer collections would fragment the signal.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up- or down-regulated in atopic dermatitis lesional skin versus control, and do those pathway calls survive exclusion of sample_01?
constraints: Use the human hallmark gene sets — organism must match the human skin data; do not use the mouse hallmark file.
Use pre-ranked GSEA over the full tested-gene ranking, not over-representation analysis on a thresholded DE list.
The gene universe / background is the set of genes tested in T1S2, not all human genes; state the universe size.
Report per-set gene coverage (members present in the 12,000-gene matrix) alongside each result.
Report NES sign convention explicitly — positive NES meaning enriched in lesional.
Run the same analysis on the T1S3 leave-one-out ranking and report concordance; do not merge the two into one result table without labelling.
steps.description: Run pre-ranked gene set enrichment against the MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC gene symbols — this reference is staged for Homo sapiens in the environment; if it is absent at run time, report that and fall back to the staged human WikiPathways or GO biological process sets, naming the substitution clearly in the output). Then repeat the identical GSEA on the leave-one-out ranking from T1S3 and report which hallmark calls are concordant in sign and significance between the two rankings. Note explicitly the number of hallmark genes that are absent from the 12,000-gene matrix, since the matrix is pre-filtered and coverage per set affects the test.
acceptance_criteria: A full hallmark result table (all 50 sets, or all sets passing the size filter) with NES, pval, padj, set size, coverage in the matrix, and leading-edge genes.
Hallmarks at padj<0.05 listed with direction, plus a summary plot and enrichment curves for the top up and down sets.
A concordance table comparing hallmark NES and significance between the full-cohort and leave-one-out rankings.
Explicit statement of the ranking statistic used, the gene universe size, and how duplicate symbols were handled.

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch, unpaired bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12,000 gene symbols x 12 samples; /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv) with a 6-vs-6 design in /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (atopic dermatitis lesional skin vs control). The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit caveat that sample_01 has ~4x lower library size than the median.

The plan therefore starts with a QC/library-size step (T1S1) that quantifies sample_01's depth, its saturation/complexity (detected genes at its depth), and its position in PCA/sample-correlation space after variance-stabilising transformation, and issues an explicit keep-or-drop recommendation with the reason. A 4x shallower library is not by itself a reason to drop a sample: DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors and negative-binomial dispersion model absorb depth differences directly, and dropping a sample from a 6-vs-6 design costs real power. The failure mode to test for is not low depth per se but low depth coupled with a compositional or complexity shift (few detected genes, outlier position on PCA, inflated Cook's distances) that indicates degraded input rather than shallow sequencing.

T1S2 runs the primary differential expression with DESeq2 on all 12 samples (~condition), which is the pre-specified primary analysis. T1S3 re-runs the identical contrast with sample_01 excluded and reports concordance of the two results — a sensitivity analysis, not a replacement. This ordering means the reported gene list is the full-cohort one, with the leave-one-out run quantifying how much sample_01 drives it, rather than the shallow sample silently deciding the result either way.

T2S1 takes the DESeq2 shrunken-LFC results and runs pre-ranked GSEA against the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets (confirmed staged for Homo sapiens), which is the pathway question asked, on the full ranked gene list rather than a thresholded subset — appropriate here because n=6 per group gives modest per-gene power and a ranked test uses the whole distribution. Hallmark GSEA is repeated on the sensitivity ranking so pathway conclusions carry the same robustness annotation as the gene-level ones.

Statistical limits to hold throughout: n=6 per group, unpaired, single batch, no covariates available in the metadata beyond condition, and only 12,000 genes present (a pre-filtered matrix), so the multiple-testing universe is smaller than a full transcriptome and enrichment background must be the tested-gene universe, not all human genes.
